plan.title: Health endpoint and HTML status page

narratives.Overview: Build a small Node.js web app that serves one HTML page and a GET /health endpoint from the same server on port 3000.
narratives.Requirements:
FR-1: GET /health returns JSON with ok=true and ts as an ISO 8601 UTC timestamp.
FR-2: The server serves one HTML page from the same port.
FR-3: The page fetches /health once on load and displays UP with the returned timestamp.
FR-4: If /health cannot be reached, the page displays DOWN and a brief error message.
NFR-1: Use plain JavaScript and Node's built-in HTTP server without a web framework.
narratives.AcceptanceCriteria:
- GET /health responds successfully with JSON containing ok=true and an ISO 8601 UTC ts.
- The HTML page loads from the same server on port 3000.
- A successful page load displays UP and the health timestamp.
- A failed health request displays DOWN and a brief error message.
narratives.Architecture: One Node.js process uses the built-in HTTP server to route GET /health and serve the HTML page.
narratives.Testing: Test the health response shape, the page's successful UP state, and the page's DOWN state when the health request fails.
narratives.Deployment: Run locally on port 3000; allow the port to be fixed at 3000 for this scope.
